summary: Reproduced the stale batch_is_full early return in the checked-out scheduler and reset the per-pass admission hint before current capacity is evaluated. Added a failing-before/passing-after regression plus zero-capacity and empty-queue boundary cases. A real single-gfx950 tiny-Llama serving probe admitted all four staggered chunked-prefill requests, including the fourth while earlier requests remained active.

tests.what_was_measured: Before-fix reproduction: stale fullness skipped current capacity/admission; all three new regression and boundary tests failed. Raw output: reports/j-17cb28bd130f/raw/regression-before.txt

After-fix scheduler regression suite: 6 passed, including stale-state reconsideration, real zero-capacity re-latching, and empty-queue behavior. Raw output: reports/j-17cb28bd130f/raw/regression-after.txt

Real HTTP/engine execution on one gfx950 GPU: four staggered 72-token prompts used 32-token chunked prefill and each generated 30 tokens; load evidence reached 4 running, 0 waiting, and the server log shows a transient queued request admitted while earlier requests remained active. The owned server process group was terminated and GPU allocations returned to zero.
Probe scripts compile and the patch has no whitespace errors.

remaining_limitations: The qualified random tiny Llama validates transport, scheduler admission, and GPU engine execution only. Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 weights and its hybrid GDN/linear-attention, mamba-state, NEXTN speculative decoding, FP8 KV, Docker/WSL2, semantic accuracy, and multi-minute production workload were unavailable and remain unverified. No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. The server required SIGKILL after its 30-second graceful-shutdown timeout; the subreaper collected descendants and a fresh Torch process reported zero allocated/reserved GPU bytes.
